274	
275	## Amendment: what the optional worktree runtime delivered, and where it departs (B35, 2026-11-10)
276	
277	The three slices are done and each was reviewed independently: `pose-optional-worktree-runtime`
278	(identity, protected endpoint, handshake, lifecycle, standalone fallback),
279	`pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache` (hosted read checks, typed results, resident memo) and
280	`pose-worktree-runtime-qos-and-measurement` (admission lanes and the measurement), with two engine
281	specs that the measurements called for (`pose-index-input-binding-reads-each-transfer-once`,
282	`pose-governance-audit-skips-pure-git-reads`). The statement above that "the runtime of slice 1
283	hosts no domain operation" was true of slice 1 only. What stands now, and what differs from the
284	decisions of this ADR:
285	
286	- **Hosted operations.** The runtime hosts five read checks (`review-check`, `closeout-check`,
287	  `artifact-check`, `surface-check`, `roadmap-check`) through `pose runtime run`, as the user that
288	  started it, in its worktree; a hosted request carries the caller's identity and is refused,
289	  before any handler runs, when it does not match the runtime's engine, build, protocol, schema
290	  or worktree; the caller's environment digest must equal the runtime's. They are not writes, but
291	  they may refresh derived files as they do standalone (published atomically); a command that may
292	  have run (deadline, lost reply) is never repeated elsewhere unasked, which is how the decision
293	  "an ambiguous committed write requires a receipt before a retry" is met for these commands.
294	  Hosted commands go through the domain's own entry (`mainCommand`), not a new typed interface:
295	  the typed-domain extraction of the first bullet of the decision stays with B31.
296	- **Caches.** The B33 views are not what the runtime reuses (the measurements showed they do not
297	  address the cost). It keeps, between commands, the output of the Git reads that are pure
298	  functions of object ids or of the commit HEAD named when they ran, keyed by the commit, the
299	  content of the shallow file and of the repository config, with a byte budget and
300	  least-recently-used eviction; no watcher exists, so "watch events are hints" is met by not
301	  using them: freshness comes from the key, and nothing about mtime or a clean tree is taken as
302	  proof. The scoped Git batch reader is untouched.
303	- **Budgets and QoS.** Admission is by two lanes (`short`, `heavy`) with slots and bounded queues
304	  and a bound on the memo; the global concurrency bound is the sum of the slots. **Not delivered:**
305	  CPU quota or affinity awareness, and per-command memory or I/O limits; the runtime bounds what
306	  it admits and keeps, not what each command consumes. The measurement records latency, the
307	  runtime's resident set and CPU time per scenario, including two simultaneous heavy checks, on one
308	  environment; it is not a general benchmark.
309	- **Platforms.** Unix domain socket on Linux and macOS (credentials of the peer from the
310	  operating system); Windows runs every command standalone and `pose runtime status` says so.
311	  The named pipe is a follow-up.
312	- **Status.** The decision stands as amended for the delivered scope; what is not delivered above
313	  is not adopted and needs its own spec before it is claimed.

14	# Spec: Limites de CPU, memória e E/S por comando hospedado
15	
16	## 1. Intent
17	
18	### Goal
19	
20	O runtime limita a CPU, a memória e a E/S que um comando hospedado pode consumir, onde a plataforma oferece (cgroups no Linux), e declara o que é suportado, configurado e efetivo.
21	
22	### Business value
23	
24	O runtime limita o que admite (faixas, filas) e o que guarda (o memo), mas não o que cada comando consome; o ADR declarou cota e afinidade de CPU como não entregues.
25	
26	### Constraints
27	
28	Rascunho escrito em 2026-11-10 a partir das pendências da sessão da B35; a spec é completada (artefatos, alvos de entrega, tarefas, validação) antes do start.

32	O que não está nos requisitos abaixo.
33	
34	## 2. Requirements
35	
36	- R1: Um limite por faixa de CPU e de memória, aplicado onde há cgroup v2, e reportado como efetivo ou não no status.
37	- R2: A afinidade de CPU (conjunto de CPUs de cada faixa) e um limite de E/S (`io.max` no cgroup v2) são configuráveis e reportados como efetivos ou não, como a CPU e a memória.
38	- R4: A medição inclui a CPU, a memória e a E/S sob o limite e um comando que o excede.
39	- R3: ADR: o limite é do processo do runtime ou de um filho por comando.
